prompt: Mailvora's analyst wants one result that reconciles November 2025, the Dublin days 1 to 30 November, in three checks. sessions: every session_start event by event_date, those of visitors who denied consent included, against the rows of sessions whose session_start falls on those Dublin days. sign-ups: every sign_up event against the rows of signups by the Dublin day of signup_ts. purchases: every purchase event against the subscriptions whose first payment (earliest paid_at) falls on those Dublin days, a first payment that was later refunded included. Return four columns, in this order: check_name (the text sessions, sign-ups or purchases), export_count, backend_count and result (the text pass when the two counts are equal, fail when they are not). Return one row for each check. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, write the purchases check: the backend side counts first payments, not every payment.
Take each subscription's earliest paid_at in a derived table, then count those that fall on a Dublin day of November.
why_this_works: Each check counts the same rows on both sides by the same Dublin days, so all three pass and the result shows it in one place.
